literal: Among the learned, learned they will be called: before the learned, things learned so as to reach, those who speak.
translation: Those who can speak what they have learned so that it reaches the minds of the learned are called the most learned among the learned.
modern: கற்ற அறிஞர்களின் முன்னே, தாம் கற்றவற்றை அவர்கள் மனத்தில் பதியும்படி தெளிவாகச் சொல்ல வல்லவர்களே, கற்றவர்களுள் சிறந்த கற்றவர்கள் என்று சிறப்பித்துச் சொல்லப்படுவார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet defines the highest tier of scholarship as the ability to communicate effectively. The phrase 'kaṟṟāruḷ kaṟṟār' means 'the learned among the learned', indicating exceptional scholars. To earn this title, one must not merely possess knowledge, but be able to speak ('colluvār') what they have learned ('kaṟṟa') before an assembly of experts ('kaṟṟār muṉ'). The crucial word here is 'cela', which literally means 'to go' or 'to reach', signifying that the speaker's words must successfully penetrate the minds of the audience and be accepted by them.
